## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components with fused spawn/render can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At N=4000 (above the L1d spill at N≈897), cost is highest — 12.736 ns/p at q=0.01 — then falls to 8.544 by N=16000 through overhead amortization. Through the L2→DRAM spill at N≈57456, cost stays FLAT: 8.544→8.369 ns/p (q=0.01) from N=16000 to N=65000, with no knee. Death rate raises the floor — ~8.35 ns/p at q=0.01, ~9.3 at q=0.05, ~13.4 at q=0.25 — without changing the N-shape. A slight rise at N≥1M appears at q=0.01 (8.351→8.779) and q=0.05 (9.299→10.336), but q=0.25 stays flat at ~13.5 ns/p throughout.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.74 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 34.7% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The algorithm is overhead-bound at small N (5.73 GB/s at N=4000) and transitions to a branch/compute-limited plateau by N=16000: ~8.7 GB/s (q=0.01), ~7.85 (q=0.05), ~5.42 (q=0.25). It never approaches the streaming ceiling at any death rate; the plateau is set by per-particle overhead, not memory bandwidth.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles. The loop advances 0x44 (68) bytes per iteration (`add x10, x10, #0x44`), with `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` and `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` operating on intra-particle floats, `ext.16b` and `mov.s v18[3]` rearranging lanes. A gather is present: `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x12]` loads one float into a single lane. The alive mask uses byte-granular `strb w11, [x24, x9]`. Per-particle branches (`fcmp`/`b.lt`, `cbz`, `cbnz`) and function calls (`bl _layouts.ML1.data.Data.spawn`, `bl _layouts.common.render_simple.splat`) for each dead particle explain the death-rate-dependent floor. No PMC data is available.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak bandwidth is 8.74 GB/s = 34.7% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling at q=0.01, N=262000. Component-wise vectorization (one particle per iteration with a `ld1.s` gather and per-particle branches) cannot stream, and death rate raises the floor from 8.35 ns/p (q=0.01) to 13.4 ns/p (q=0.25) via per-particle `bl spawn`/`bl splat` calls. The hypothesis fails even in the low-churn regime.
